title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela
lab: Facebook AI Research; University College London; New York University
date: May 2020 (arXiv v1, 22 May 2020); v4 April 2021; published at NeurIPS 2020

code.title: transformers-research-projects/rag
code.note: the authors' Hugging Face port (fine-tuning and evaluation scripts; Apache-2.0). Transformers moved its examples/research_projects folder, where the old page's link pointed, to this separate repository in 2025 (the folder's README now says so), so that link returns 404 (checked 2 October 2026); the models themselves are RagSequenceForGeneration and RagTokenForGeneration in Transformers. About 20 minutes for the README and entry path

run_label: ask the trained toy RAG model
takeaway: Coined RAG: a DPR retriever and a BART generator trained end to end, the retrieved documents treated as a latent variable and marginalised (RAG-Sequence against RAG-Token); state of the art on open-domain QA, and knowledge updated by swapping the index, not the weights.
verdict: Believe the mechanism, the hot-swap and the factuality gain; of the four open-domain QA "state of the art" claims two are clear (Natural Questions by about 2.6 standard errors, TriviaQA-Wiki) and two sit inside the noise (WebQuestions, CuratedTrec), and every result is one run.

headline.d: against 41.5 for DPR's extract-and-rerank pipeline and 36.6 for closed-book T5-11B+SSM
2016 leaders answered with a 2016 index, against the 2018 index: knowledge updated with no retraining

headline.k: judged more factual, RAG against BART
headline.d: human evaluation of Jeopardy question generation

resources.t: Meta AI blog: Retrieval Augmented Generation
resources.n: the authors' own framing; short and good on the motivation of hot-swapping the index instead of retraining.
the original model as runnable code (RagSequenceForGeneration, RagTokenForGeneration, RagRetriever over the wiki_dpr index); the clearest way to see how the pieces compose (core pages).

the released RAG-Token checkpoint fine-tuned on Natural Questions; the paper's demo address, huggingface.co/rag, now redirects here (checked 2 October 2026), so the interactive demo is gone. Its twin is facebook/rag-sequence-nq.

resources.t: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
resources.n: the standard bridge from this paper to the modern stack; its Naive, Advanced and Modular RAG taxonomy is the usual map of what the field became (survey).

resources.t: How to Build an Open-Domain Question Answering System?
resources.n: places RAG among the 2020 retriever-reader and retriever-generator systems (DrQA, ORQA, REALM, DPR, FiD) with their equations side by side.
a visual walk through RETRO, the 2021 descendant that moved retrieval inside the network with chunked cross-attention.

kb.n: the DPR retriever is a pair of BERT-base encoders; retrieval embeddings remain BERT's main living habitat.

kb.t: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
kb.n: the same month's parametric-only counterpoint; GPT-3-style in-context learning is what later let deployed RAG drop this paper's end-to-end training.
retrieval moved from a fixed pipeline step to a tool an agent decides to call: the road to agentic RAG.

kb.t: T5: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning
kb.n: the closed-book baselines of Table 1 are T5 models (fine-tuned by Roberts et al., with salient span masking for T5+SSM).
the generator (BART) and both retriever encoders (BERT) are Transformers; the toy generator on this page is built like that page's toy model.

topics.n: this is the founding paper of the topic.
